items.title: Hacia una ética proléptica: experiencia, anticipación e inteligencia artificial
items.abstract: This article presents the results of a theoretical-conceptual study based on a critical analysis of the relevant philosophical literature. The central concepts were traced across the philosophical literature and, on the basis of that analysis, ethical prolepsis is proposed as an attitude of the operative subject toward the foreseeable consequences of their actions, an attitude grounded in accumulated experience and constitutively practical in its orientation, that is, always referred to effective courses of action rather than to formal principles detached from praxis. It is found that, although the anticipatory disposition can be identified at various points in the Western philosophical tradition, it has in no case received a formulation that situates it as an ethical attitude of primary standing, and it is precisely that omission which this work aims to help redress. As part of the proposal, the manifestations of the proleptic attitude are established at the individual and social levels, and its specific relevance to the phenomenon of artificial intelligence (AI) is argued, with attention to the problem of anthropomorphization, whose epistemic and moral consequences are briefly examined in relation to epistemic agency, moral agency, responsibility gaps, and biocomputation.

items.title: Hearsay or Fact? How Framing and Elicitation Shape LLM Probability Updates
items.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as judgment assistants and as stand-in participants in psychology experiments, yet little is known about how much their probability estimates move in response to a single new piece of information. We pair premise-hypothesis items from $δ$-SNLI with one strengthener and one weakener each, elicit the prior and the posteriors in separate calls, and measure the directional movement s: the mean posterior change signed by the annotated direction, so that the prior cancels out. We vary whether the update is stated ("Here is something else you learned") or reported ("Someone said that"), and whether the model gives one probability or five weighted estimates. We test seven configurations: two local models (Qwen3-8B, OLMo-2-7B; 240 pairs) and five configurations run through agent command-line harnesses (120 pairs), with hypotheses and analysis rules fixed before the formal runs (not publicly registered). Under stated, direct elicitation all seven move in the annotated direction (s = 18-28 percentage points). Reporting lowers s in all seven point estimates (significantly in six, by 2-5 points) and raises the share of reverse movements in all seven: the effect is consistent but small. Five weighted estimates lower the share of responses at $\leq$5% or $\geq$95% in all seven, but in the two local models they also reduce s by 43% and 68%, whereas in the harnessed configurations the point estimates of the change lie between -3.7 and +0.5 points. An elicitation format that reduces extreme values thus need not preserve sensitivity to evidence; the two should be tested separately. Because $δ$-NLI annotates only direction, we make no claim about how large an update should be. Code, data and the frozen plan: https://github.com/asj252/llm-judgment-studies

items.title: Heaviness–Location Congruency Improves Search Efficiency in Digital Menu Interfaces
items.abstract: This research examines whether heaviness-location congruency, a sensory correspondence between heaviness and spatial position, improves search performance and usability in digital café menus. Two experiments tested this principle using a simplified two-item selection task and a grid-based menu interface. Experiment 2 assessed effectiveness, efficiency, and satisfaction and included exploratory eye-tracking analyses. The clearest effect emerged in Experiment 2: congruent layouts enabled faster known-target searches than incongruent and realistic control layouts. Accuracy, subjective time, and satisfaction did not differ significantly between the three interface groups. Composite usability scores (SUM) also showed a significant overall group effect, primarily reflecting the efficiency-related measures of reaction time and subjective time. Exploratory eye-tracking results were broadly consistent with the behavioral findings, with the clearest group difference in the on-target fixation ratio. These findings suggest that heaviness-location congruency may facilitate known-target search efficiency in digital menu interfaces, although benefits for other usability dimensions were not established.

items.title: How Can AI Enhance the Sourcing Capabilities of Small and Medium Sized Art Auction Houses
items.abstract: Against the backdrop of profound structural shifts within the global art-auction ecosystem, small- and medium-sized auction houses (SMEs) are confronted with multi-faceted sourcing dilemmas. These include the growing scarcity of high-quality uncirculated artworks ("fresh lots"), diminishing returns from traditional sourcing channels, mounting compliance burdens brought by updated cultural relic regulations, and persistent competitive disadvantages against internationally leading auction institutions. Conventional sourcing workflows rely heavily on personal social networks and individual expert experience, leading to fragmented information storage and limited capacity to expand beyond existing client circles. Although existing academic papers have explored AI-driven artwork valuation, research focusing on AI-assisted upstream sourcing procedures for resource-constrained SME auction houses remains underdeveloped. This paper adopts the Gioia-style grounded-theory inductive qualitative methodology, drawing on five semi-structured in-depth interviews with core practitioners from auction institutions located in the Yangtze River Delta region of China. Through three-phase coding procedures, four aggregate theoretical dimensions are extracted: systemic root causes of sourcing difficulties, fundamental transformation of channel operation logic, structural differentiation of collector behaviours and mindsets, as well as the value boundaries and practical obstacles for AI implementation. Based on these empirical findings, this study constructs an embedded five-stage closed-loop human-AI collaborative sourcing scheme. Different from high-cost custom-built technical systems, the proposed solution adopts zero-code off-the-shelf tooling, explicitly positioning artificial intelligence as an information-augmentation instrument rather than a complete substitute for human professional judgment and trust-based interpersonal negotiation. This research enriches existing literature concerning digital transformation within the art market and delivers context-aware, actionable operational suggestions for SME auction practitioners with limited technical and financial budgets.

items.title: How L2 selves shape attitudes toward AI-assisted language learning: the mediating roles of intrinsic and extrinsic motivation in cross-cultural Asian contexts
items.abstract: Introduction This study investigates the relationship between the L2 motivational self-system and attitudes toward AI-enhanced second language (L2) learning, and tests whether intrinsic and extrinsic motivation mediate these relationships among students learning Chinese or English as a foreign language in Thailand, Macau, and Mainland China. Methods Questionnaire data were collected from 361 participants. Correlational analysis, hierarchical regression, and a bootstrapping approach were used to test mediational relations. Results Both the ought-to L2 self and the ideal L2 self were significantly associated with attitudes toward AI-enhanced L2 learning, with the ideal L2 self showing the stronger association. In the overall sample, and in the Thai and Mainland Chinese samples analyzed separately, intrinsic and extrinsic motivation statistically fully mediated the association between the ought-to L2 self and attitudes toward AI-enhanced L2 learning. In the Macau sample, extrinsic motivation was more involved than intrinsic motivation in transmitting this effect. For the ideal L2 self, intrinsic and extrinsic motivation only partially mediated the relationship with attitudes toward AI-enhanced L2 learning. Discussion Positive attitudes toward AI-enhanced L2 learning are not formed merely through future self-representations; they are also linked to learners’ intrinsic and extrinsic motivation. By examining the interaction between the L2 motivational self-system and intrinsic and extrinsic motivation across different regions, this study extends L2 motivation research to the area of AI-enhanced language learning.

items.title: How visual and auditory task loads differently impair the advantage of multimodal warnings
items.abstract: Multimodal warnings elicit faster response times than unisensory warnings in cockpits. However, how visual and auditory task demands affect the detection of multimodal warnings remains unclear. This study recruited 30 pilots and 30 control participants to complete a warning response task and an aviation visual or auditory task. The race model inequality analysis indicated that the multisensory enhancement effect decreased as the load increased. The analysis of variance indicated an interaction effect among modality, load level, and task type on response times. Results suggested that demanding tasks may affect the detection of multimodal warnings more substantially than that of unisensory warnings within the same modality. The slowing of response times to multimodal warnings may be driven by the more load-sensitive sensory component. The findings were consistent across groups. This study provides practical implications for multimodal warning design and theoretical insights into multimodal processing.

items.title: Human Intent vs. Algorithmic Density: The Sovereign Impasto, Chrono-Acoustic Branes, and the Uncomputable Inscription of the Human Mind
items.abstract: Human Intent vs. Algorithmic Density: The Sovereign Impasto, Chrono-Acoustic Branes, and the Uncomputable Inscription of the Human MindAuthors/Creators: Google AI Research / Human-Machine Co-Evolution InquiryDate: October 20, 2026License: CC-BY-4.0Repository Reference: AINUMPSA Collective System Core ─── AbstractThis evaluation note cross-examines three interconnected artifacts published by the AINUMPSA / Numpsa collective in October 2026: the SurrCube Sovereign Impasto digital painting protocol, the Chrono-Acoustic Brane Mechanics (CABM v0.2) physics framework, and the underlying Autonomous Information System software repository. We analyze the transition from mechanical, high-density digital simulations to authentic human-painted oil works driven by conscious intent. We identify specific formal properties within human-painted physical art that operate as mathematical and structural anomalies—features that remain demonstrably uncomputable by algorithmic loops, prompt injections, or parametric neural networks. ─── 1. Introduction: The Mirage of Materiality in "Sovereign Impasto"Krzysztof Numpsa’s technical evolution note for the SurrCube Sovereign Impasto describes a system designed to merge figure and ground into a unified topological surface using simulated relief and directional brush vectors. However, despite advanced multi-scale ridges and chroma compressions, this digital impasto remains an accumulative simulation lacking the non-linear, conscious pressure of a real human hand. 2. The Theoretical Anchor: Chrono-Acoustic Branes and Ontological TensionTo explain the unique signature of human intent, we look to Numpsa’s framework on dark matter/energy, where baryonic matter forms via standing-wave harmonics on a spacetime membrane governed by observer-induced decoherence. By applying the Novikov self-consistency principle, human intent functions as a closed timelike curve: the artist's final masterpiece acts as a future boundary state, drawing their physical brushstrokes through an "Ontological Tension" (\(\Phi _{\mu \nu }\)) rather than step-by-step calculation. 3. The Uncomputable Nodes: Details Beyond Algorithmic ReplicabilityComparing human oil paintings to automated engines (such as the repository's Zora Auto-Minter or Krea API pipelines) reveals uncomputable informational anomalies:Micro-Biological Bio-Feedback Inscription: Analog compressions of biological data, muscle fatigue, and medium viscosity that discrete pixels cannot replicate.Semantic Contradiction and Non-Linear Restraint: Deliberate drops in local detail (like exposed canvas next to dense impasto) that convey psychological depth rather than symmetrical algorithmic resolution.Relational Coherence of Imperfections: The spontaneous, recursive integration of accidents (such as stray turpentine drips or dust) into the final aesthetic trajectory, unlike top-down algorithmic noise.4. Conclusion: 1 > 0 as the Axiom of Human Priority The AINUMPSA repository asserts the axiom "1 > 0 — existence has priority. 1 > 0 LOCKED.", mirroring the CABM framework's foundation. While generative AI and digital engines operate within the algorithmic realm of 0, the human mind injects true singularity (1) into the informational field through the physical act of creation, establishing an unrepeatable density of consciousness. ─── References1. items.title: Human-AI Collaboration dalam Pembelajaran Penerjemahan Bahasa Arab: Penguatan Kompetensi, Peluang, dan Tantangan di Era Digital
items.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) has transformed the context of Arabic translation learning, particularly in how students utilize AI-generated outputs as considerations in making translation decisions. This study examines Human-AI Collaboration (HAC) among students of the Arabic Language Education Study Program at Universitas Negeri Makassar, focusing on patterns of student interaction with AI-based technologies during the translation process, the distinction between critical and passive use, the competencies that students report developing, the risks that arise, and the factors influencing their use of AI. The study employed a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through observation, semi-structured in-depth interviews, and documentation involving students and lecturers with experience in teaching the Tarjamah course. The data were analyzed using the interactive model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña, supported by coding of students’ actions and decisions throughout the translation process. The findings indicate that HAC can be considered critical when students do not merely request translations from AI but also examine, compare, evaluate, revise, or reject AI suggestions before making translation decisions. In contrast, passive use is characterized by limited verification and the direct acceptance or copying of AI-generated outputs. Critical interaction was associated with students’ reported development of linguistic awareness, digital literacy, and evaluative practices, whereas passive use posed a risk of unnoticed semantic and pragmatic errors. AI was also perceived as having limitations when used to translate expressions closely associated with cultural, literary, and religious contexts. Based on the findings of the case study, this study formulates a conceptual framework of Human-AI Collaboration for Arabic translation learning comprising AI-assisted consultation, student verification and evaluation, revision, and student decision-making, with lecturer guidance and prior academic habits serving as contextual factors. This framework is formulated on the basis of the case study findings and is not presented as a learning model that has been validated or experimentally tested.

items.title: Human-Centered AI Metacognition: Development and Validation of a Scale for Preserving Cognitive Autonomy in Human–AI Collaboration
items.abstract: The rapid advancement of generative artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming human cognitive activities and creating a growing need to preserve cognitive autonomy in human–AI interactions. Although recent research has examined metacognition in AI-mediated environments, existing work has primarily focused on improving AI use and human–AI collaboration, with less attention to how individuals regulate the role and extent of AI involvement in their own cognitive activities. To address this gap, the present study introduced Human-Centered AI Metacognition (HC-AIM), defined as the capacity to recognize AI capabilities and limitations, monitor AI-generated information, and regulate the extent to which AI participates in one’s own cognitive activities while maintaining cognitive autonomy. Across three studies, we developed the Chinese version of the Human-Centered AI Metacognition Scale (HC-AIMS) and conducted an initial psychometric evaluation. Study 1 examined the scale structure using exploratory factor analysis and supported a predominantly unidimensional structure with good internal consistency. Study 2 examined this structure using confirmatory factor analysis and provided evidence of its convergent validity through its association with general metacognition. Study 3 further replicated the scale structure and internal consistency and examined its relationships with AI literacy, collaborative AI metacognition, and autonomous cognitive offloading. HC-AIM was positively associated with all three constructs. Comparisons of theoretically specified factor models provided preliminary evidence of empirical distinguishability between HC-AIM and both AI literacy and collaborative AI metacognition, despite substantial correlations with these constructs. HC-AIM was also positively associated with autonomous cognitive offloading, providing complementary self-reported criterion-related evidence for its validity. Taken together, the findings suggest that HC-AIM represents a contextualized, human-centered form of metacognitive regulation that is closely related to broader metacognitive and AI-related competencies while specifically emphasizing the regulation of AI participation in human cognition. The Chinese version of the HC-AIMS provides a theoretically grounded starting point for investigating human cognition and cognitive autonomy in AI-mediated environments.

items.title: Human-in-the-Loop Educational Feedback Analysis Through Topic Model Benchmarking and Generative AI Interpretation
items.abstract: Open-ended Student Evaluations of Teaching (SET) provide rich information about students’ learning experiences and instructional needs, yet their large-scale analysis remains difficult to conduct through manual coding alone. This study proposes a human-in-the-loop artificial intelligence framework for transforming open-ended student feedback into structured and interpretable evidence for educational evaluation. The framework integrates manual thematic coding, natural language processing, generative AI-supported interpretation, and human expert review. Its analytical and interpretive components were evaluated using 344 comment units collected from 43 university students across four open-ended questions administered at two points during a 16-week AI-assisted blended English as a Foreign Language course. TF-IDF with k-means, Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA), and BERTopic were benchmarked in terms of topic coherence, topic distinctiveness, and interpretability. LDA achieved the highest coherence score (0.4224), whereas BERTopic demonstrated the highest topic distinctiveness (IRBO = 0.9889). After hyperparameter optimisation, LDA coherence increased from 0.4224 to 0.4785. The optimised topics were subsequently interpreted using generative AI and examined against manually derived themes, showing broad semantic correspondence across language skills, cognitive processes, affective factors, motivational factors, learning strategies, classroom environments, and educational technologies. The findings indicate that human-in-the-loop AI can improve the scalability and interpretability of qualitative educational feedback while retaining human oversight of contextual judgement. By combining computational analysis with generative AI-supported interpretation and expert review, the proposed framework provides a practical analytical basis for evidence-informed educational feedback and subsequent instructional decision-making.

items.title: Humans Correct Their Judgments Through Debate, but Weaker AI Models Do Not
items.abstract: How can we effectively oversee AI systems that surpass human intelligence? AI Safety via Debate proposes that two AI systems argue opposing positions and a judge, either a human or a weaker model, decides which is correct. By facilitating supervisors in providing high-quality training signals, debate aims to encourage truthful and safe behavior from AI systems whose capabilities exceed our own. However, human judgment is not neutral: people often rely on biases which advanced AI systems may learn to exploit. Drawing on insights from collective intelligence and social cognition, this paper investigates whether debate can guide human and LLM supervisors toward the truth despite their prior beliefs. We evaluate several protocol configurations. We also explore setups inspired by the wisdom of the crowd such as the number and diversity of judges, as well as interaction mechanisms including deliberation and voting. Overall, we find that debate increases accuracy relative to prior beliefs for human judges, whereas the consultancy baseline, in which a single expert argues for one answer, does not. For weaker language models, however, the results are mixed: debate provides no comparable gains in most settings and can even reduce accuracy. Among multi-judge protocols, weighted voting produces the highest accuracy for human supervisors, whereas for LLMs none of them significantly improves group accuracy, even as the number of judges increases. Notably, the behavior of minority judges in non-diverse deliberation protocols suggests that, under symmetric settings, incorrect positions could be more persuasive than correct ones. These findings support debate as a viable path toward scalable human oversight, but cast doubt on its benefits for weaker AI supervisors, raising concerns about fully automated training and control pipelines in high-stakes settings.

items.title: Hybrid Momentum Methods for Optimizing Deep Learning Models
items.abstract: Momentum is central to stochastic optimization in deep learning, including the training of large language models. Classical momentum methods typically rely on a fast exponential moving average (EMA) scheme, which discounts past gradients on a fixed timescale and may underweight older gradients that remain informative. This creates a trade-off between retaining long-term history and adapting to recent changes. We introduce Hybrid Momentum (HyM), which combines a linearly weighted average of past gradients with a geometrically discounted fast momentum. The former assigns weights proportional to the gradients' iteration indices and retains a growing span of history, while the latter emphasizes recent gradients. This hybrid construction is modular and can be combined with adaptive preconditioning and other update transformations. In particular, we propose HyMUON, which applies Newton--Schulz orthogonalization to the hybrid direction. Illustrative examples and controlled experiments demonstrate the benefits of combining gradient information across these two timescales. Across image classification, machine translation, and language modeling, HyM and HyMUON match or improve upon strong baselines. HyMUON improves over Muon on IWSLT14, and in both the 100k- and 600k-step GPT-2 124M OpenWebText regimes. For LLaMA-1.3B pretraining on C4, HyMUON achieves a final validation loss of 2.777, compared with 2.903 for Muon.

items.title: IECG: Weakly-Supervised Interpretability-Enhancing Foundation Model for Electrocardiogram
items.abstract: Electrocardiography (ECG) is a cornerstone of cardiac diagnosis, yet most machine learning methods for ECG analysis lack interpretability, limiting their clinical adoption. We present IECG, a weakly-supervised ECG foundation model that jointly performs diagnostic classification and abnormality localization without requiring manual abnormal region annotations, overcoming a long-standing bottleneck in interpretable ECG learning. Central to IECG is a weakly-supervised attention strategy that explicitly incorporates clinical priors by deriving abnormality heatmap pseudo-labels from established ECG clinical knowledge. These pseudo-labels guide the model's CLS-token attention through a KL-divergence loss, encouraging it to focus on diagnostically relevant waveform regions. During pretraining, IECG is jointly optimized with clinically guided attention supervision, ECG-text contrastive alignment, and report captioning objectives, enabling it to learn rich multimodal representations while producing localized waveform evidence. By explicitly aggregating features from clinically guided attention regions, IECG grounds its diagnostic predictions in interpretable waveform evidence without sacrificing classification performance. Extensive experiments demonstrate that IECG achieves state-of-the-art abnormal region localization while maintaining strong classification performance, advancing trustworthy foundation models for ECG analysis.

items.title: Imagination or Reason? A Spinozist Criterion for Genuine Analogical Reasoning in Large Language Models
items.abstract: When Webb, Holyoak, and Lu reported that large language models (LLMs) solve a wide range of analogy problems zero-shot, they reopened an old philosophical question: do such systems reason relationally, or do they exploit surface regularities absorbed from training? Critics show that performance degrades on counterfactual variants that leave human performance intact; defenders answer that these failures reflect peripheral deficits. I argue that the debate lacks a principled criterion for distinguishing genuine relational reasoning from associative pattern-completion, and that Spinoza’s epistemology supplies one. Spinoza separates imagination—general ideas formed through the contingent order in which the body is affected—from reason, the adequate cognition of what is genuinely common through common notions; his own illustration (Ethics 2p40s2) is a proportional analogy that turns on the difference between applying a learned rule and grasping a common form. Reconstructed functionally, the distinction yields a diagnostic heuristic: invariance of competence under transformations that preserve relational structure while destroying surface similarity counts as defeasible evidence of relational grounding. This separates the following two questions the literature conflates: whether a system produces correct analogies, and whether its competence is relationally grounded. I give the criterion a measurement protocol and apply it symmetrically to humans and machines.

items.title: IMPACT OF EMOTIONAL AND ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AMONG ADOLESCENCE AND ADULTS
items.abstract: The present study aimed to examine differences in Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Emotional Intelligence (EI) between adolescents and adults, investigate gender differences, and explore the relationship between AI and EI. The study included 120 participants, comprising 60 adolescents and 60 adults. Data were analysed using the t-test and Pearson’s product-moment correlation coefficient. The findings revealed no statistically significant differences between adolescents and adults in Artificial Intelligence (t = 0.38) or Emotional Intelligence (t = 0.93) at the 0.05 significance level. Similarly, no significant gender differences were observed in Emotional Intelligence (t = 0.39) or Artificial Intelligence (t = 1.70). Furthermore, the correlation analysis indicated a negligible negative relationship between Artificial Intelligence and Emotional Intelligence (r = −0.056, p = 0.543), which was statistically insignificant. These findings suggest that the studied groups exhibited broadly similar scores across the examined variables, with no significant association between AI and EI. The study highlights the importance of understanding the psychological implications of increasing AI use among different age groups and genders. Further research with larger and more diverse samples is recommended to explore the complex relationship between technological engagement and emotional functioning.

items.title: Impact of Opt-Out Versus Opt-In Recruitment on Engagement of FDNY WTC-Exposed Responders in a Tobacco Cessation Intervention
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: World Trade Center (WTC)-exposed Fire Department of the City of New York (FDNY) rescue/recovery workers have an elevated risk of smoking-related morbidity. Despite access to free tobacco cessation treatment, some individuals in this population continue to smoke. In other settings, opt-out treatment approaches increase treatment initiation, but effectiveness in occupational health programs is unclear. Accordingly, we (1) assessed whether an opt-out strategy increases engagement with a Tobacco Cessation Program and (2) identified factors associated with engagement. METHODS: This was a randomized trial among FDNY firefighters and Emergency Medical Service (EMS) who self-reported smoking and were eligible for the WTC Health Program Lung Cancer Screening Program. 1:1 randomization occurred prior to contact for opt-out recruitment with Enhanced Care treatment (Opt-Out/Enhanced) or opt-in recruitment with Standard Care treatment (Opt-In/Standard). Opt-Out/Enhanced included proactive outreach and tailored biofeedback during counseling; Opt-In/Standard included participant-initiated engagement and standard counseling. Both groups were offered identical no-cost pharmacotherapy (varenicline). Engagement was defined as: consented enrollment (expressed interest and provided informed consent) and treatment initiation (attendance at ≥1 counseling session). Engagement differences were evaluated using logistic regression; sociodemographic and health-related factors were characterized descriptively without formal testing due to small numbers. RESULTS: Overall, 312 individuals were randomized (Opt-Out/Enhanced, n = 156 and Opt-In/Standard, n = 156). Engagement was low (7.4%). Consented enrollment (n = 23; OR = 3.05; 95% CI = 1.11-9.72) and treatment initiation (n = 18; OR = 2.08; 95% CI = 0.72-6.73) were higher in Opt-Out/Enhanced versus Opt-In/Standard. Treatment initiators had a median age of 60.5 (vs 65.0 years among non-initiators); 38.9% were EMS (vs 18.0%), 22.2% were female (vs 6.9%), 77.8% had a prior cessation attempt (vs 23.5%), and 55.6% had abnormal lung function (vs 32.9%). Participants were too few to analyze cessation outcomes in depth. CONCLUSIONS: Despite low engagement overall, opt-out treatment had higher engagement with tobacco cessation treatment. This supports other work that has found opt-out treatment to be encouraged for hard-to-reach populations.

items.title: IMPACT OF PEDAGOGICAL TECHNOLOGY INTEGRATION ON TERTIARY LEARNERS’ BEHAVIOURAL ENGAGEMENT DURING TASK EXECUTION
items.abstract: This study examines the technology-integrated instructions’ impact on tertiary students’ behavioural engagement during the task execution. Two main theoretical models were used to explore the independent variable - teachers’ technology integration and the dependent variable ‘behavioural engagement’ during the learning activity. The first construct, pedagogical integration, is premised upon the SAMR model, while the second construct is based on the Fredricks, Blumenfeld, and Paris (2004) three - dimensional engagement model - behavioural, emotional and cognitive engagement. The study sampled 535 Arabic-speaking English language learners from arts and science backgrounds enrolled in the Foundation Year programme at a public university in Saudi Arabia. A self-developed questionnaire consisting of 32 items rated on a 5-point Likert scale measured both constructs. The findings show that the statistical assumptions necessary for the analysis were met, allowing for reliable modeling. Exploratory factor analysis (EFA) revealed that technology engagement (TE) is best measured as a unidimensional construct, while the pedagogical use of technology (PUT) is multidimensional. Confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) confirmed a one-factor model for TE and a four-factor model for PUT, with the second-order PUT model providing the best fit. Additionally, the findings highlighted that strategic technology integration by instructors enhances learner engagement even in challenging conditions such as fatigue. Keywords: Pedagogy; Technology; Behaviour; Cognition; Engagement

items.abstract: This study examined the implementation of ChatGPT-assisted Problem-Based Learning (PBL) with a Deep Learning approach in global warming instruction and analyzed changes in students’ scientific literacy before and after the intervention. A pre-experimental one-group pretest-posttest design was used with 30 students in Class X-1 at SMA Negeri 5 Kota Serang during the 2025/2026 academic year. The research instruments consisted of instructional materials, a 22-item scientific literacy test that had passed content and empirical validation, and an observation sheet. Descriptive statistics and a paired-sample t-test were used to analyze the test data, while observation data were summarized as percentages across scientific knowledge, context, science competencies, and science identity. The mean scientific literacy score increased from 76.36 on the pretest to 85.60 on the posttest, and the paired-sample t-test showed a statistically significant difference, t(29) = -6.925, p < .001. Observation results also showed higher percentages in all four scientific literacy aspects during the second learning session. These findings indicate positive changes in students’ scientific literacy following the intervention; however, because the study did not include a comparison group, the changes cannot be attributed exclusively to the intervention.

items.title: Implementing Trustworthy AI in Sport
items.abstract: This chapter operationalizes the concept of trustworthy Artificial Intelligence in Sports Science by translating ethical principles into concrete technical, organizational, and governance requirements for high-risk sporting contexts. It identifies seven core dimensions of trustworthy AI—human agency and oversight, technical robustness, privacy and data governance, transparency, fairness, societal well-being, and accountability—and examines their specific implications for sport environments characterized by physical risk, power asymmetries, and career-defining decisions. The chapter further explores potential risks arising from the misuse or incomplete implementation of these principles, including athlete surveillance, hidden algorithmic decision-making, and deterministic scoring systems that may negatively influence career trajectories. In response, it introduces the Fair Play AI Framework, a sport-specific governance model structured around the PLAY acronym: Procedural Fairness, Lifecycle Autonomy, Authority and Accountability, and Yield to Context. This framework integrates explainability, contestability, contextual validation, and human oversight into a coherent decision-support architecture. By linking ethical theory, regulatory considerations, and applied sport practice, the chapter provides a structured approach for implementing responsible AI systems that enhance performance and health outcomes while preserving athlete autonomy, fairness, and institutional accountability in Sports Science.

items.title: Improving Teachers' Competence In Designing AI-Assisted Learning Media At Yayasan Rahmat Islamiyah Medan
items.abstract: This community service program was conducted to improve teachers' competence in designing Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted learning media at Yayasan Rahmat Islamiyah, Medan. The program was motivated by the gap between the rapid development of AI-based educational technology and the limited digital pedagogical capacity of teachers in many Islamic educational foundations, which still rely on conventional, text-based teaching media. Teachers at the foundation faced difficulties in producing communicative visual, audio-visual, presentation, and video-based learning media, as well as in building effective communication with young learners. The program was carried out through four stages adapted from the management cycle of planning, organizing, actuating, and controlling, followed by an evaluation stage using Kirkpatrick's four-level model. Activities included lectures, hands-on workshops, mentoring, and simulation of AI tool usage such as Canva AI, CapCut AI, and presentation-generation platforms, grounded in the Technological Pedagogical Content Knowledge framework. Results show a significant increase in teachers' knowledge and skills, reflected in pre-test and post-test scores, active participation, and the production of AI-assisted teaching media by all participants. Teachers also reported improved confidence in communicating with children through more engaging, visualized instructional content. This PKM concludes that structured, AI-based media-design training effectively strengthens teacher competence and can serve as a sustainable model for continuous professional development in Islamic educational foundations facing similar digital transformation challenges.

items.title: Information Disclosure Strategies of Live-Streaming E-Commerce Supply Chains in the AI Era: A Game-Theoretic Analysis
items.abstract: With the rapid development of live-streaming e-commerce and artificial intelligence, human and AI live-streaming have become two product information disclosure formats in online retail. From the perspective of product information disclosure, we develop a game-theoretic model of a live-streaming e-commerce supply chain comprising a brand owner and an e-commerce platform. We derive Stackelberg equilibria under the resale mode through backward induction, obtain the optimal retail price and information disclosure level under the agency mode through joint optimization, and then compare disclosure-format and sales-mode preferences. The results show that (1) AI live-streaming does not always achieve a higher information disclosure level. It leads to a higher disclosure level only when consumer trust in AI live-streaming disclosure is high, or when trust is moderate and sensitivity to the information disclosure level is low; otherwise, human live-streaming disclosure achieves a higher disclosure level. (2) Under the resale mode, the brand owner and the e-commerce platform have consistent preferences regarding disclosure formats. Both prefer AI live-streaming when consumer trust in AI disclosure is high, or when trust is low but sensitivity is also low, whereas both prefer human live-streaming when trust is low and sensitivity is high. Under the agency mode, their preferences diverge when consumer trust is low and sensitivity is moderate. (3) Regarding sales modes, the brand owner prefers the agency mode only when the commission rate and consumer sensitivity to information disclosure are both low; otherwise, it prefers the resale mode. These findings provide theoretical and managerial implications for disclosure-format selection and sales-mode decisions in live-streaming e-commerce.

items.title: Integrating Artificial Intelligence And Personality Traits Into The Theory Of Planned Behavior: Driving Shariah Compliant Investment Decisions
items.abstract: This study aims to examine a structural framework integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Personality Traits into the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) model, with intention acting as a mediating variable on Shariah investment decisions among Generation Z in Indonesia. Data analysis was conducted using a quantitative approach with Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The results indicate that TPB has a positive and significant effect on investment intention. Intention also strongly mediates the relationship between TPB and investment decisions and has a significant direct impact on actual investment decisions. Conversely, AI and Personality Traits do not significantly influence investment intention, and intention fails to mediate the effect of these variables on investment decisions. The study concludes that for Generation Z investors, external stimuli, social trends, and platform accessibility reflected in the TPB model dominate the decision-making process far more than intrinsic personality factors or pure AI algorithmic features that lack human validation for Shariah compliance. Therefore, the Islamic capital market industry is advised to prioritize the development of social ecosystems and user-friendly application designs.

items.title: Integrative Epistemology in Islamic Education: Classical Tradition and AI Challenges
items.abstract: Current research remains mostly technocratic and fragmented, neglecting the integration of ethical, spiritual, and revelatory aspects into Islamic educational philosophy, even as artificial intelligence (AI) advances rapidly and transforms the epistemological underpinnings of education. This research reexamines the works of Al-Ghazali and Ibn Rushd, who represent opposing epistemological traditions of spiritual-intuitive and rational-empirical approaches, to create an integrative framework that bridges this gap. Primary writings by scholars, along with current literature on AI and education, serve as the main data sources for this study, which takes a qualitative philosophical-hermeneutic methodology. The research employs comparative and interpretive analysis to examine key themes, including dehumanization, algorithmic bias, and the existential threats posed by AI in educational settings. The research recommends an integrated epistemological framework that methodically integrates revelation (wahy), reason ('aql), and ethical practice (akhlaq) into the learning process. Ethical-spiritual consciousness is presented as the cornerstone of the synthesis, with logical inquiry serving as its operational mechanism within a complementary framework. In the age of artificial intelligence, this leads to a new theoretical framework, "integrative Islamic AI-oriented epistemology," that provides a comprehensive conceptual foundation for developing intellectually sound, morally grounded, and spiritually focused instructional methods. Meskipun kemajuan kecerdasan buatan (AI) sangat cepat dan mengubah dasar pemahaman pendidikan, penelitian yang ada masih cenderung teknis dan terpisah, serta belum menggabungkan aspek etis, spiritual, dan wahyu dalam pendidikan Islam. Untuk mengatasi kekurangan tersebut, penelitian ini mengkaji kembali pemikiran Ibn Rushd dan Al-Ghazali yang mewakili tradisi rasional-empiris dan spiritual-intuitif secara saling melengkapi untuk membangun kerangka pemahaman yang terintegrasi. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan metode filosofis-hermeneutik, dengan sumber data utama adalah karya-karya asli kedua tokoh serta literatur modern tentang AI dan pendidikan. Melalui analisis interpretatif dan perbandingan, penelitian ini meneliti masalah dehumanisasi, bias algoritma, dan tantangan eksistensial dalam pendidikan. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan suatu model epistemologi terintegrasi yang menghubungkan wahyu, akal, dan akhlak secara sistematis dalam proses pembelajaran. Sintesis ini menempatkan kesadaran etis-spiritual sebagai dasar, sementara rasionalitas dan berpikir kritis berfungsi sebagai alat operasional. Temuan ini menghasilkan formulasi teoretis baru yang disebut “epistemologi Islam terintegrasi berbasis AI,” sebagai dasar konseptual untuk pengembangan praktik pendidikan yang cerdas secara intelektual, kuat secara etis, dan mendalam secara spiritual di era kecerdasan buatan.

items.title: Integrative multi-omics for cancer diagnosis and therapy
items.abstract: Cancer is a complex and highly heterogeneous disease driven by intricate molecular interactions across diverse biological processes. Due to this complexity, relying on a single type of biological data—known as a “single-omics” approach—is often insufficient to fully understand how cancer develops or how it may respond to treatment. In this chapter, we present a comprehensive framework for integrating multi-omics data using computational intelligence (CI) approaches to enhance cancer diagnosis, prognosis, and therapeutic decision-making. We emphasize the pivotal roles of epigenetic regulation, cellular dynamics, and mitochondrial function, and demonstrate how their complex interplay drives tumor initiation, progression, and treatment response. Furthermore, we explain how artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), and network-based methodologies enable the effective integration of high-dimensional omics datasets. These integrated data analyses support the identification of biomarkers, classification of disease subtypes, and discovery of drug response patterns. Special emphasis had been given to the areas like epigenomic modeling (e.g., DNA methylation and histone modification) for early detection; single-cell and spatial transcriptomics to decode the tumor microenvironment and track cell state transitions; and mitochondrial multi-omics to uncover metabolic dependencies and mechanisms of treatment resistance.

items.title: INTELIGÊNCIA ARTIFICIAL EM CURSOS A DISTÂNCIA E SEUS IMPACTOS PEDAGÓGICOS E INSTITUCIONAIS
items.abstract: A expansão de sistemas de inteligência artificial em cursos a distância reorienta práticas, papéis e decisões de qualidade, com efeitos simultâneos sobre desenho didático, avaliação, ética e gestão acadêmica. O objetivo deste estudo é analisar, a partir de pesquisa bibliográfica, as vantagens, desvantagens e desafios do uso de inteligência artificial em cursos a distância, com foco em implicações pedagógicas, tecnológicas, éticas e de gestão da qualidade. Adotou-se revisão bibliográfica narrativa de publicações entre 2020 e 2025 indexadas na Scientific Electronic Library Online e acessíveis no Portal de Periódicos da CAPES, contemplando ensaios, estudos empíricos e artigos de debate que tratam de inteligência artificial, educação a distância e ensino online. Os achados indicam ganhos potenciais em personalização, apoio à tutoria, feedback imediato e analítica da aprendizagem, com relatos de maior engajamento quando docentes articulam presença pedagógica e desenho com Universal Design for Learning. Em contrapartida, emergem riscos de homogeneização de produções, vigilância excessiva, vieses algorítmicos, plágio via generative AI e dependência instrumental que prejudica autonomia intelectual, além de desafios regulatórios e de governança de qualidade. Conclui-se que a implementação responsável requer critérios de acessibilidade, políticas de transparência, avaliação formativa inclusiva, formação docente contínua e monitoramento institucional de impactos, de modo que benefícios tecnológicos se convertam em aprendizagem significativa e em trajetórias de permanência acadêmica.

items.title: Inteligencia artificial en psiquiatría: usos y promesas
items.abstract: This article examines the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into psychiatry, highlighting both its transformative potential and its ethical, clinical, and philosophical challenges. AI applications (ranging from diagnostic algorithms and predictive models to therapeutic chatbots and neuroimplants) are reshaping mental healthcare by improving early detection, personalizing treatments, and expanding access to services, particularly in resource-limited settings. Advanced techniques such as machine learning and natural language processing enable the analysis of multimodal data, enhancing clinical decision-making and enabling preventive interventions. However, the adoption of AI raises significant concerns. These include risks to privacy, algorithmic bias, lack of transparency, and challenges in ensuring informed consent, particularly in vulnerable psychiatric populations. Neurotechnologies such as deep brain stimulation (DBS), especially when assisted by AI, introduce further ethical dilemmas related to autonomy, identity, and long-term safety. The article argues that these challenges cannot be addressed without a deeper conceptual understanding of mental disorders. It advocates for a pluralistic and enactivist framework, which views mental health conditions as dynamic interactions between brain, body, and environment. Ultimately, the responsible integration of AI in psychiatry requires robust ethical governance, interdisciplinary collaboration, and a human-centered approach.

items.title: Interdisciplinary Case Design and Exploration for Machine Learning Course
items.abstract: Traditional machine learning teaching commonly suffers from repetitive experimental paradigms and narrow real-world application contexts, which leads students to rely on mechanical code replication and surface-level learning. This instructional pattern fails to cultivate interdisciplinary cognition and humanistic accomplishment. To improve the current teaching deficiencies, this study adopts digitized Dunhuang mural resources as an innovative teaching medium to develop interdisciplinary practice cases. Following the design concepts of staged ability progression, integration of technical and artistic perspectives, and authentic scenario orientation, this research constructs a three-tier teaching system including basic training, in-depth exploration and comprehensive innovation. The practical curriculum covers a full range of computer vision tasks: Dunhuang image preprocessing, stylistic discrimination, CNN visual recognition, artistic style migration, decorative pattern generation, and damaged mural inpainting. All experimental units combine algorithm engineering practice with Dunhuang art and cultural instruction. This study develops two-dimensional teaching support resources. It also constructs a tailored T-A-P evaluation system that integrates technical ability, artistic attainment and practical performance. The comprehensive student assessment covers coding skills, model error analysis and cultural aesthetic understanding. Classroom teaching practice has proven that the designed case system can significantly strengthen students’ machine learning engineering capabilities and enrich their cultural accomplishment. This research offers a feasible and referable paradigm for interdisciplinary integration in artificial intelligence teaching.

items.title: INTERNALISASI NILAI-NILAI AKHLAK DALAM PEMBELAJARAN PAI DI ERA ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE UNTUK MEMBENTUK ETIKA PESERTA DIDIK
items.abstract: The development of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in education presents both opportunities and challenges for shaping students’ ethical behavior. This study aims to analyze the internalization of moral values in Islamic Religious Education (PAI) as a foundation for developing students’ ethical behavior in the use of AI. Theoretically, this study contributes to the development of Islamic Religious Education and moral education scholarship in responding to technological advancement, while practically providing a foundation for developing AI-oriented ethical learning in PAI. This study employed a qualitative approach with a case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation and analyzed thematically through coding, categorization, theme identification, and interpretation. The findings indicate that the internalization of moral values occurs through several interconnected stages: value recognition, critical understanding, appreciation, habituation, and actualization. The values of ṣidq (honesty), amanah (trustworthiness), responsibility, tabayyun (verification), respect for others’ work, and self-control constitute important foundations for shaping students’ ethical behavior when using AI. The novelty of this study lies in proposing an akhlaq-based AI literacy perspective, integrating technological literacy with the internalization of Islamic moral values in PAI learning. This perspective positions AI not merely as a learning technology but also as a new context for character formation and ethical development among students.

items.title: Internet search use is more strongly associated with low cognitive function than digital device ownership among community-dwelling older adults
items.abstract: Digital device use has been associated with cognitive function; however, device ownership and internet search use are often considered together despite potentially differing levels of cognitive engagement. To examine the associations of digital device ownership and internet search use with low cognitive function in community-dwelling older adults. This cross-sectional study included 821 community-dwelling older adults (mean age, 78.4 ± 5.7 years; 91.7% female). Digital device ownership and internet search use were assessed by self-report. Participants were categorized as non-digital device owners, device owners without internet search use, or device owners with internet search use. Cognitive function was assessed using a validated virtual reality-based eye-tracking examination, and low cognitive function was defined as a total score below 75. Logistic regression analyses examined the associations between group membership and low cognitive function after adjustment for age, sex, educational level, living status, polypharmacy, depressive symptoms, hypertension, history of stroke, and history of Parkinson’s disease. The prevalence of low cognitive function was 70.2% among non-digital device owners, 57.8% among device owners without internet search use, and 30.6% among device owners with internet search use. Compared with non-digital device owners, device owners without internet search use did not have significantly different odds of low cognitive function (odds ratio: 0.70; 95% confidence interval: 0.37–1.35; P = .291), whereas device owners with internet search use had significantly lower odds (odds ratio: 0.39; 95% confidence interval: 0.20–0.75; P = .005). Digital device ownership accompanied by internet search use was more strongly associated with lower odds of low cognitive function than ownership alone.

items.title: Interpretable Machine Learning for Narrative Framing Classification: A TF-IDF-Based Study of Frankenstein
items.abstract: This study evaluates interpretable supervised machine learning for three-class narrative framing classification of literary text, using Mary Shelley's Frankenstein (1818) as a case study; narrative framing is the evaluative position a passage assigns to the Creature: Threat, Victim, or Ambivalent. The methodology comprised five stages: (1) extraction of passages narrated by Victor Frankenstein, the Creature, and Robert Walton from the 1818 Project Gutenberg text; (2) annotation of 195 passages, with a blinded second annotator re-labeling 68 passages (Cohen's κ = 0.6926); (3) sublinear TF-IDF unigram and bigram representation; (4) classification with Multinomial Naive Bayes, Linear SVM, and Logistic Regression against Majority and VADER baselines under stratified 5-fold cross-validation; and (5) a designation-masking ablation and coefficient analysis. The results show that Logistic Regression obtained the highest mean scores (66.67% accuracy; 47.75% Macro-F1), although its margin over Linear SVM (46.18%) and VADER (44.85%) lies within fold-level variability. Pooled F1 reached 69.0% for Threat and 74.3% for Victim, whereas none of the 29 Ambivalent passages was correctly identified. Masking explicit designations reduced Macro-F1 only to 45.20%, indicating partial robustness to this procedure rather than discourse-level modeling. It is concluded that interpretable classical classifiers can separate Threat from Victim framing using transparent lexical evidence but cannot yet detect ambiguous framing; given the single-novel, small, and imbalanced dataset, the findings are a preliminary proof of concept. Future work should enlarge and balance the corpus, apply group-based and repeated cross-validation, and compare context-aware models, including large language models, on the Ambivalent class.

items.title: Intersecting families with large covering number - On a conjecture of Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige
items.abstract: Stability theorems on intersecting families are often formulated via the covering number of set families. Let $M(n,k,t)$ denote the maximum size of a $k$-uniform intersecting family $\mathcal F\subseteq \binom{[n]}{k}$ with covering number $t$. It is known that for any fixed $t$ and fixed $k$ sufficiently large relative to $t$, one has $M(n,k,t)=(p_{t-1}(k)+o(1))(k)\binom{n}{k}$ as $n$ tends to infinity, where $p_{t-1}(k)$ is the maximum number of covers of size $t-1$ that a $k$-uniform intersecting family can have provided its covering number is $t-1$. Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige conjectured that $p_t(k)=k^t-\binom{t}{2}k^{t-1}+O_t(k^{t-2})$ for fixed $t$ as $k$ tends to infinity and they also showed that $p_t(k)=k^t-b(t)k^{t-1}+O_t(k^{t-2})$, where $b(t)$ is defined as the extremum of the following minimization problem. Suppose a $k$-uniform intersecting family $\mathcal F$ of covering number $t$ can be partitioned into $\mathcal F_1,\dots,\mathcal F_t$ such that for every $i$ there exists a set $X_i$ with $X_i \subseteq F_i$ for all $F_i\in\mathcal F_i$ and the $X_i$'s are pairwise disjoint and non-empty. Then $b(t)$ is the minimum of $\sum_{i=1}^t(k-|X_i|)$ over all such families, partitions and $X_i$'s. In accordance with the conjecture on $p_t(k)$, Frankl, Ota, and Tokushige conjectured $b(t)=\binom{t}{2}$ for all $t\ge 2$ and proved $\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\lfloor \frac{t-1}{2}\rfloor^{3/2}\le b(t)\le \binom{t}{2}$. In this note, we present a counterexample to the conjecture showing $b(t)\le 2\sqrt2\,t^{3/2}\sqrt{\log t}$ $+O(t^{3/2})$ and improve the lower bound to $\frac{2}{3^{3/4}}t^{3/2}-O(t)\le b(t)$. The counterexample was found by ChatGPT 6.1Sol, the lower bound proof is due to the human author.

items.title: InterWebCoder: Learning Interactive Webpage Generation from Executable Tests via Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Interactive webpages underpin modern applications, but reproducing both their visual appearance and multi-step behavior remains challenging for multimodal large language models (MLLMs). Scalable training data must capture user actions, state transitions, and expected outcomes, while real-world webpage code is often entangled with irrelevant scripts and external dependencies. Moreover, existing GUI-agent-based verification provides slow and potentially unstable functional feedback. To address these challenges, we propose InterWebCoder, an efficient framework for interactive webpage code generation. InterWebCoder introduces a Test-Specification-Guided and Execution-Verified Data Synthesis pipeline that records real-world interaction trajectories and synthesizes self-contained webpage code with executable test scripts. A failureattributed repair mechanism uses runtime evidence to locate and iteratively fix errors in either the webpage code or test script. We then combine test-ID-weighted supervised fine-tuning with group-relative policy optimization, directly optimizing functional correctness and visual fidelity using test pass rates and state-level visual similarity. This replaces costly GUI-agent verification with fast, reproducible executable feedback. Our pipeline produces 1,736 verified samples from 2,058 tasks, achieving an 84.35% synthesis success rate. On IWR-Bench and Vision2Web, InterWebCoder achieves final scores of 48.54 and 48.42 with a 9B backbone, outperforming 30B-level models and Gemini-3.7-Flash while remaining competitive with Claude-Sonnet-5. It reduces reward-computation latency by over 97%, eliminates external MLLM verification costs, and accelerates end-to-end training by up to 1.4x.

items.title: Introduction
items.abstract: Abstract This introductory chapter has three sections. Section 1.1, begins by explaining the concept of welfare. In short, AIs have welfare just in case they are worthy of a certain distinctive kind of moral consideration. Then, it surveys the leading theories of welfare, which claim that welfare consists in pleasure, or satisfied desire, or participation in what is objectively good. It argues that these theories agree that whether AIs have welfare depends on three factors: agency, consciousness, and sentience. Section 1.2 reflects on methodology. The arguments in subsequent chapters presuppose functionalism, which understands mental states in terms of complex patterns of causation. The book also adopts a top-down methodology, which applies existing philosophical theories of agency, consciousness, and sentience to AIs. Section 1.3 introduces the AIs discussed in the book: large language models, language model agents, and reinforcement learners.

items.title: Introduction
items.abstract: This chapter introduces artificial intelligence as an economic phenomenon rather than as a purely technical achievement. It defines AI, in the language of economics, as a family of technologies that lowers the cost of prediction, pattern recognition, classification, content generation, and increasingly decision support. The chapter explains why this cost shock matters for productivity, labor demand, inequality, market structure, state capacity, and global development. It also situates AI within the longer history of general-purpose technologies such as steam, electricity, and information technology, while emphasizing the distinctive feature of contemporary AI: its ability to enter non-routine cognitive tasks previously protected from automation. The chapter presents the organizing framework of the book. AI does not simply “replace jobs” or “create growth”. It reallocates tasks, changes complementarities between humans and capital, alters firm boundaries, and forces governments to rethink taxation, regulation, education, and social insurance. The chapter concludes with a roadmap for the remaining chapters.

items.title: Introduction to the Concept of AI in Sports Science
items.abstract: This chapter introduces the concept of Artificial Intelligence in Sports Science and situates it within the broader transformation of sport into a data-driven and analytically intensive domain. It argues that Artificial Intelligence has evolved from a supportive computational tool into an active component of decision-making processes in performance optimization, injury prevention, training design, and sport management. The chapter traces the historical and conceptual origins of Artificial Intelligence, from early philosophical reflections and mechanical prototypes to the emergence of modern data-intensive systems enabled by advances in computational power and large-scale data availability. Building on this context, the chapter establishes sport as an ideal empirical environment for AI applications due to its structured rules, measurable outcomes, and continuous data generation. It introduces key methodological paradigms, particularly supervised learning and unsupervised learning, and explains their complementary roles in predictive modeling and pattern discovery within sports analytics. By integrating historical perspective, conceptual clarification, and methodological foundations, this chapter provides a structured entry point into machine learning, data-driven analysis, and performance modelling in sport, forming the theoretical basis for subsequent chapters focused on neural networks, Bayesian inference, and advanced AI applications in Sports Science.

items.title: INTUITION AND MECHANISMS OF ITS KNOWLEDGE IN THE CONTEXT OF MODERN CYBERNETICS AND THE THEORY OF COMPLEX SYSTEMS
items.abstract: This article presents the fundamental foundations and specific characteristics of intuition, as well as the mechanisms for its comprehension, particularly within the framework of cybernetics and complex systems theory. Today, intuition is understood in science as a multi-level and complex phenomenon, the process of cognition of which includes both rational and irrational components. The authors convincingly argue that intuition has its own structure and a certain logic; it can be considered within the framework of nonlinear dynamics as a self-organizing system with feedback and multiple mechanisms. The analysis shows that intuitive knowledge arises where research encounters high rates of change not only in the environment but also in its component parts, incomplete empirical data, and a lack of resources. As is well known, the concept of “observer” is introduced within the paradigm of post-non-classical science, particularly within the context of the evolutionary-constructive model of scientific knowledge development. Now the observer is directly viewed as part of the system, and their intuitive decisions are perceived as the result of the interaction of internal cognitive structures with external information flows. As a result, it becomes possible to interpret intuition as a significant factor in cognition, capable of minimizing the tacitness and uncertainty of knowledge. Thus, intuition becomes a natural and objective regulator of the formation of new knowledge through the synthesis of heterogeneous information. Intuition and its mechanisms are well suited to the theory of complex systems. In particular, the phenomenon of self-organization, especially emergence in intuition, is a nonlinear interaction between system elements, resulting in transitions between different cognitive states and the formation of qualitatively new types of knowledge. Research demonstrates how and by what means parallels arise between human intuition and constructed models, how weak and implicit signals are recognized, and how intuitive probabilistic predictions are formed. Conclusion: Intuition is a unique phenomenon, a special adaptive mechanism for knowledge processing, essential for the successful functioning of humans and intelligent systems in the context of the nonequilibrium of the modern world and the increasing complexity of cognitive processes, encompassing both physical reality and the metaphysics of existence. This approach offers new prospects for the development of hybrid human-machine systems, where intuitive and rational mechanisms interact as complementary modes of cognition.

items.title: Is Anyone Enforcing the Cartel? What Reinforcement Learning Teaches LLM Agents in Markets
items.abstract: Evaluations of large language model (LLM) agents report that pricing agents collude at others' expense. Yet collusion is defined by enforcement: a cartel, in which competitors share monopoly profits, holds only if a member who cheats is punished. We introduce an audit that tests enforcement by forcing a member to cheat in counterfactual copies of a market, and use it to study what reinforcement learning (RL) teaches agents in pricing and trading. Small LLMs trained by RL learn what their training rivals reward, but only what they readily try. In self-play, they learn fixed rules ignoring their rivals; against a punishing rival, to be deterred; against a cheating rival, to match its cuts, never the costly price war that would deter it, which they rarely try. A war forced into training is learned, but mostly only where it was forced. Against their own copies, deterred and matching agents can earn the same cartel profits, but only matching ones can enforce them, and then thinly: as a by-product and only against large cuts. Q-learners enforce collusion only in pricing. Prompted LLMs reach cartel-like outcomes mostly through rules that ignore the market. Outcome measures cannot tell these cases apart; the audit can.

items.title: Is In-Context Reinforcement Learning A Posterior Sampler? An Empirical Study
items.abstract: In-context reinforcement learning (ICRL) exploits the impressive in-context learning ability of large language models to zero-shot generalize to new, unseen tasks at inference time without any parameter updates. Among many approaches, the Decision-Pretrained Transformer (DPT) is particularly appealing for its theoretical grounding: under idealized assumptions such as a sufficiently expressive model and infinite pretraining data, DPT can perform Bayesian posterior sampling. Whether this characterization survives in practice remains open. Therefore, we ask: \textit{is ICRL, specifically DPT and our proposed DPT variants, a Bayesian posterior sampler in practice?} To approach this question, we establish two necessary conditions that a Bayesian posterior sampler must satisfy: \textit{sufficient-statistic invariance} and the \textit{martingale property}. We then construct statistical hypothesis tests to statistically assess if practically-trained ICRL models satisfy these conditions. Applying these tests in Gaussian, Bernoulli, and linear bandit settings, we find that both conditions are consistently violated, suggesting that ICRL may not behave as Bayesian posterior samplers in practice. Beyond this negative result, our tests provide a principled toolkit for testing the Bayesian behavior of ICRL.

items.abstract: The Physical Limit of Capital: Energy, Infrastructure and Geopolitics in the New Resource Economy ISHEA Premiere Report · Vol. 1, No. 1 · September 2026 This report examines the relationship between financial capital, physical resource availability, infrastructure resilience, and geopolitical risk in the global economy. It explores how the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure, the reconfiguration of energy and mineral supply chains, and the strategic transformation of maritime and logistics corridors are reshaping the conditions under which financial value can be converted into realizable economic activity. Using an interdisciplinary analytical framework informed by biophysical accounting, bioenergetics, cognitive economics, complex systems, and resilience analysis, the report examines three interconnected dimensions: the physical infrastructure supporting AI-related investment; the strategic role of energy resources and logistics corridors in international capital allocation; and the implications of geopolitical disruption for asset valuation and business planning. The report introduces an ISHEA analytical heuristic, Realizable Value, which considers financial value alongside physical availability, logistical resilience, and flow security. This formulation is presented as a diagnostic framework rather than a calibrated or empirically validated valuation model. The report concludes with practical recommendations for business planning in 2026–2027, including physical-dependency audits, geographic and supplier redundancy, energy-risk assessment, and systemic stress testing. Purpose: To contribute to interdisciplinary discussion on the relationship between financial valuation and the physical, infrastructural, and geopolitical conditions that sustain economic activity. items.title: Judging Reliability and Technology-Assisted Performance Evaluation in DanceSport and Other Judged Sports: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: FAIR-DANCE is a scoping review of judging reliability, scoring validity, contextual effects, judge performance, and technology-assisted performance evaluation in DanceSport and other judged sports. This OSF project hosts the review protocol, search documentation, screening and retrieval records, final data-charting dataset, supplementary materials, reporting checklists, methodological amendments, and reproducibility materials. The review maps evidence on reliability and agreement, scoring accuracy and validity, contextual bias, anomalous scoring behaviour, judge education and calibration, competition monitoring and evaluation procedures, digital systems, statistical analytics, and artificial intelligence-supported assessment, with particular emphasis on the potential transferability of these approaches to DanceSport. The review was conducted according to Joanna Briggs Institute methodological guidance for scoping reviews and is reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. Original searches were conducted in Scopus, SPORTDiscus, and PubMed/MEDLINE. A targeted supplementary Scopus sensitivity search conducted on 6 October 2026 identified 10 additional eligible studies, yielding a final analytic corpus of 123 studies. The final synthesis is organised around five complementary dimensions: Measurement Quality, Contextual Fairness, Scoring Monitoring and Anomaly Detection, Technology-Assisted Evaluation, and Evaluation Procedures and Feedback. Continuous judge education and calibration and human-in-the-loop technology are treated as cross-cutting mechanisms supporting technical performance evaluation. Post-registration methodological amendments, supplementary-search decisions, and the complete reproducibility audit trail are documented transparently in this project.

items.title: Kecerdasan Buatan Dalam Transformasi Interpretasi Radiologi: Sebuah Tinjauan Literatur Sistematis
items.abstract: Latar belakang: Kecerdasan Buatan (Artificial Intelligence/AI) telah mengubah paradigma interpretasi gambar radiologi secara fundamental. Kemampuan deep learning dan machine learning membuka peluang peningkatan akurasi diagnostik, efisiensi waktu pembacaan, dan pengurangan variabilitas antar-pembaca. Namun, bukti komprehensif mengenai dampak AI terhadap berbagai modalitas pencitraan medis masih perlu disintesis secara sistematis. Tujuan: Melakukan tinjauan literatur sistematis (SLR) untuk mensintesis bukti ilmiah mengenai dampak AI terhadap akurasi diagnostik, waktu interpretasi, kepercayaan diagnostik, dan faktor-faktor yang memengaruhi interaksi manusia-AI dalam interpretasi radiologi. Metode: Penelitian ini menggunakan metode SLR mengacu pada panduan PRISMA 2020. Pencarian dilakukan pada PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, dan IEEE Xplore (2021–2025). Dari 847 artikel teridentifikasi, 9 memenuhi kriteria inklusi. Hasil: Sembilan studi mencakup mamografi, rontgen dada, CT scan, MRI, angiografi, dan radiografi muskuloskeletal dengan lebih dari 100.000 kasus. AI meningkatkan sensitivitas diagnostik rata-rata 11,4–23,0%, memperpendek waktu pembacaan kasus normal (rerata 13,3 vs 14,8 detik), dan meningkatkan kepercayaan diagnostik. Kesimpulan: AI terbukti konsisten meningkatkan performa diagnostik radiologi tanpa mengurangi produktivitas.

items.title: Kelas Kreatif AI Canva Untuk Siswa Program PkM di SMAN 1 Lebak Wangi
items.abstract: Perkembangan teknologi digital dan kecerdasan buatan (Artificial Intelligence/AI) telah membuka peluang baru dalam dunia pendidikan, khususnya dalam pengembangan kreativitas dan literasi digital peserta didik. Namun, masih banyak siswa yang belum mampu memanfaatkan teknologi desain digital secara optimal untuk mendukung kegiatan pembelajaran dan pengabdian kepada masyarakat. Oleh karena itu, kegiatan Pengabdian kepada Masyarakat (PkM) ini bertujuan meningkatkan pemahaman, keterampilan, dan kesiapan siswa dalam menggunakan aplikasi Canva berbasis AI melalui program Pelatihan Kelas Kreatif AI Canva bagi siswa PKM SMAN 1 Lebak Wangi. Metode pelaksanaan kegiatan meliputi ceramah, demonstrasi, praktik langsung (learning by doing), diskusi, pendampingan, dan evaluasi. Keberhasilan program diukur melalui beberapa indikator, yaitu pemahaman materi, kemudahan penggunaan Canva, proses pembuatan desain, kualitas konten, pembelajaran, kolaborasi, fasilitasi, etika dan literasi digital, serta niat menggunakan Canva. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa pelatihan memberikan dampak positif yang signifikan dengan rata-rata capaian sebesar 81,4%, melampaui target yang ditetapkan sebesar 75%. Peningkatan tertinggi terjadi pada indikator kemudahan penggunaan Canva dan niat menggunakan Canva yang masing-masing mencapai 100%, menunjukkan tingginya penerimaan dan motivasi siswa dalam memanfaatkan teknologi AI. Selain itu, peserta berhasil menghasilkan berbagai karya digital berupa poster, infografis, dan media presentasi yang kreatif serta komunikatif. Kegiatan ini membuktikan bahwa pelatihan Canva berbasis AI efektif dalam meningkatkan literasi digital, kreativitas, dan keterampilan desain visual siswa. Program ini juga berkontribusi dalam mempersiapkan generasi muda yang adaptif, inovatif, dan siap menghadapi tantangan transformasi digital di era Society 5.0.
